records.source: :mod:`spacr.ports` now declares what each module consumes and produces, and :mod:`spacr.artifacts` records where every finished run put its outputs.  This module joins the two:
records.translation: :mod:`spacr.ports` deklarerar nu vad varje modul konsumerar och producerar, och :mod:`spacr.artifacts` registrerar var varje avslutad körning lade sina utdata.  Den här modulen förenar de två:

records.context: :func:`chained_inputs` asks the registry — ``latest(kind, project=…)`` — where the upstream module's output *is*, and turns that into the value a setting name should hold.  The answer comes from the row the producer wrote, not from re-deriving ``<root>/merged``;
records.label: spacr.chaining#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: :func:`chained_inputs` asks the registry — ``latest(kind, project=…)`` — where the upstream module's output *is*, and turns that into the value a settings key should hold.  The answer comes from the row the producer wrote, not from re-deriving ``<root>/merged``;
records.translation: :func:`chained_inputs` frågar registret — ``latest(kind, project=…)`` — var uppströmsmodulens utdata *finns*, och omvandlar det till det värde som en inställningsnyckel ska ha.  Svaret kommer från raden som producenten skrev, inte från att ``<root>/merged`` härleds på nytt;

records.context: :func:`resolve_settings` applies those values to a settings key-value mapping **without ever overwriting a path the user edited**.  A user edit is remembered in a :class:`PinStore` and takes precedence until it is cleared; when the upstream later moves, the new location is *offered* (:class:`HeldPin`) rather than pushed;
records.label: spacr.chaining#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: :func:`resolve_settings` applies those values to a settings dict **without ever overwriting a path the user edited**.  A user edit is remembered in a :class:`PinStore` and takes precedence until it is cleared; when the upstream later moves, the new location is *offered* (:class:`HeldPin`) rather than pushed;
records.translation: :func:`resolve_settings` tillämpar dessa värden på en inställningsordbok **utan att någonsin skriva över en sökväg som användaren har redigerat**.  En användarredigering sparas i en :class:`PinStore` och har företräde tills den rensas; när uppströmsdata senare flyttas *erbjuds* den nya platsen (:class:`HeldPin`) i stället för att tvingas på;

Only when no run was ever registered does the declared layout in :data:`spacr.ports.PORTS` answer instead, and then it answers with the folder the ports say it is in.
records.translation: Upplösningen är densamma som den automatiska kedjningen utför. För varje indata som modulen deklarerar tillfrågas registret först — :meth:`spacr.artifacts.Registry.latest` för den typen i det projektet, så som :func:`chained_inputs` frågar — så att ett släpp och en automatisk kedjning fyller fältet med samma sträng. records.source: 1. **a pinned value wins.**  If the user has typed a path for this key, it is restored and is not overwritten by a newer upstream run, a different plate or a restart.  When the upstream has moved since, the move is reported in :attr:`Resolution.held` for an interface to *offer*; 2. otherwise, a value already in ``settings`` that is not a placeholder wins.  Loading a settings CSV, dropping a folder or seeding from another screen all land here, and none of them is overridden within the same session; 3. otherwise the registry's answer is used.
records.translation: 1. **ett fäst värde vinner.**  Om användaren har skrivit in en sökväg för denna nyckel återställs den och skrivs inte över av en nyare uppströmskörning, en annan platta eller en omstart. Att läsa in en inställnings-CSV, släppa en mapp eller förifylla från en annan skärm hamnar alla här, och inget av dem åsidosätts inom samma session; 3. annars används registrets svar.

records.context: **Every download is atomic, and never overwrites.** Bytes stream into a temporary file *in the destination directory* (so the final ``os.replace`` is a same-filesystem rename, which is atomic) and the rename happens only after the checksum passes. An interrupted or cancelled download therefore leaves nothing behind that looks like a model — the failure mode where half a checkpoint sits at the real filename, loads, and segments badly, cannot happen.

records.context: There is no ground truth here. :func:`benchmark` runs one model over N microscope fields of view and reports what came out: object counts, timings and the :mod:`spacr.seg_qc` verdict per microscope field of view (fused? shattered? empty? all on the border?). That is a *quality-control* score, not an accuracy — it can tell you a model collapsed on your data, it cannot tell you which of two plausible segmentations is right. :data:`RANK_KEYS` therefore offers exactly two structured-data names, ``'qc'`` and ``'seconds'``, and no structured-data name that would read as accuracy. To compare two models against each other, use :func:`compare_entries`, which hands both to :func:`spacr.model_compare.compare_models` — the A/B harness that is explicit about neither side being the truth.
records.label: spacr.model_zoo#18
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: There is no ground truth here. :func:`benchmark` runs one model over N fields and reports what came out: object counts, timings and the :mod:`spacr.seg_qc` verdict per field (fused? shattered? empty? all on the border?). That is a *quality-control* score, not an accuracy — it can tell you a model collapsed on your data, it cannot tell you which of two plausible segmentations is right. :data:`RANK_KEYS` therefore offers exactly two keys, ``'qc'`` and ``'seconds'``, and no key that would read as accuracy. To compare two models against each other, use :func:`compare_entries`, which hands both to :func:`spacr.model_compare.compare_models` — the A/B harness that is explicit about neither side being the truth.
records.translation: Det finns ingen facit här. :func:`benchmark` kör en modell över N bildfält och rapporterar vad som kom ut: objektantal, tidsåtgång och utlåtandet från :mod:`spacr.seg_qc` per bildfält (sammanslaget? sönderslaget? tomt? allt vid kanten?). Det är en poäng för *kvalitetskontroll*, inte en noggrannhet — den kan tala om för dig att en modell kollapsade på dina data, men den kan inte avgöra vilken av två rimliga segmenteringar som är rätt. :data:`RANK_KEYS` erbjuder därför exakt två nycklar, ``'qc'`` och ``'seconds'``, och ingen nyckel som skulle kunna läsas som noggrannhet. För att jämföra två modeller mot varandra, använd :func:`compare_entries`, som lämnar båda till :func:`spacr.model_compare.compare_models` — den A/B-testrigg som uttryckligen anger att ingen av sidorna är facit.

records.translation: Skyddsåtgärder

records.context: **Every download is checksummed, and verification happens before use.** A checkpoint truncated by a dropped connection, or swapped for a different one at the same URL, still loads. It does not throw; it produces silently different masks, and the run that used it looks exactly like the run that did not. So :func:`fetch` hashes what arrived and compares it to the hash the catalogue published: a mismatch deletes the file and throws :class:`ChecksumMismatch` — the entry is never registered. The hash that was actually computed is stored on the returned entry, so "verified" means "these bytes", not "this filename".
records.label: spacr.model_zoo#9
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Every download is checksummed, and verification happens before use.** A checkpoint truncated by a dropped connection, or swapped for a different one at the same URL, still loads. It does not raise; it produces silently different masks, and the run that used it looks exactly like the run that did not. So :func:`fetch` hashes what arrived and compares it to the hash the catalogue published: a mismatch deletes the file and raises :class:`ChecksumMismatch` — the entry is never registered. The hash that was actually computed is stored on the returned entry, so "verified" means "these bytes", not "this filename".
records.translation: **Varje nedladdning kontrollsummeras, och verifieringen sker före användning.** En checkpoint som trunkerats av en bruten anslutning, eller bytts ut mot en annan på samma URL, går ändå att läsa in. Den utlöser inget undantag; den ger tyst annorlunda masker, och körningen som använde den ser exakt ut som körningen som inte gjorde det. Därför hashar :func:`fetch` det som anlände och jämför det med hashen som katalogen publicerade: en avvikelse tar bort filen och utlöser :class:`ChecksumMismatch` — posten registreras aldrig. Hashen som faktiskt beräknades lagras på den returnerade posten, så "verified" betyder "these bytes", inte "this filename".

records.context: ``'none'`` no hash at all — nothing can be checked, and :func:`fetch` refuses such an entry unless the caller overrides it. ``'published'`` a hash came with the entry but the bytes are not here yet; it is the digest the download will be checked against. ``'recorded'`` the hash of the file on disk is known, but no published digest exists to compare it against. It shows only that the file has not changed since the hash was recorded. ``'verified'`` the bytes on disk were compared with a published digest and match.
records.label: spacr.model_zoo.ModelEntry.checksum_state#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``'none'`` no hash at all — nothing can be checked, and :func:`fetch` refuses such an entry unless the caller overrides it. ``'published'`` a hash came with the entry but the bytes are not here yet; it is the digest the download will be checked against. ``'recorded'`` the hash of the file on disk is known, but no published digest exists to compare it against. It shows only that the file has not changed since the hash was recorded. ``'verified'`` the bytes on disk were compared with a published digest and match.
records.translation: ``'none'`` ingen hash alls — inget kan kontrolleras, och :func:`fetch` vägrar en sådan post om inte anroparen åsidosätter det. ``'published'`` en hash följde med posten men byten finns inte här ännu; det är sammanfattningen som nedladdningen kommer att kontrolleras mot. ``'recorded'`` hashen för filen på disken är känd, men ingen publicerad sammanfattning finns att jämföra den med. Det visar bara att filen inte har ändrats sedan hashen registrerades. ``'verified'`` byten på disken jämfördes med en publicerad sammanfattning och stämmer överens.

records.context: The rules, in order:
records.label: spacr.model_zoo.classify_kind#1

records.source: The rules, in order:
records.translation: Reglerna, i ordning:

records.context: 1. ``*.CP_model`` is a Cellpose checkpoint — that is what :func:`spacr.submodules.train_cellpose` names its output. 2. ``*.pth`` / ``*.pt`` is a machine-learning classification model checkpoint (:func:`spacr.io._save_model` writes ``<model_type>_epoch_<n>_channels_<ch>.pth``) **unless** it sits in a Cellpose folder or has ``cellpose``/``cp_model`` in its name. 3. An **extensionless** file inside a Cellpose folder is a Cellpose checkpoint only if its first bytes are a torch save. ``cellpose.train`` writes ``<save_path>/models/<name>`` with no suffix, and that folder also holds READMEs and logs — the magic-byte check is what keeps a ``README`` out of the zoo. 4. Anything else is not a model. CSVs, PNGs, ``.npy`` masks and settings snapshots all land here and are ignored.
records.label: spacr.model_zoo.classify_kind#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: 1. ``*.CP_model`` is a Cellpose checkpoint — that is what :func:`spacr.submodules.train_cellpose` names its output. 2. ``*.pth`` / ``*.pt`` is a classifier checkpoint (:func:`spacr.io._save_model` writes ``<model_type>_epoch_<n>_channels_<ch>.pth``) **unless** it sits in a Cellpose folder or has ``cellpose``/``cp_model`` in its name. 3. An **extensionless** file inside a Cellpose folder is a Cellpose checkpoint only if its first bytes are a torch save. ``cellpose.train`` writes ``<save_path>/models/<name>`` with no suffix, and that folder also holds READMEs and logs — the magic-byte check is what keeps a ``README`` out of the zoo. 4. Anything else is not a model. CSVs, PNGs, ``.npy`` masks and settings snapshots all land here and are ignored.
records.translation: 1. ``*.CP_model`` är en Cellpose-checkpoint — det är så :func:`spacr.submodules.train_cellpose` namnger sina utdata. 2. ``*.pth`` / ``*.pt`` är en klassificerarcheckpoint (:func:`spacr.io._save_model` skriver ``<model_type>_epoch_<n>_channels_<ch>.pth``) **såvida inte** den ligger i en Cellpose-mapp eller har ``cellpose``/``cp_model`` i sitt namn. 3. En fil **utan filändelse** i en Cellpose-mapp är en Cellpose-checkpoint endast om dess första byte är en torch-sparning. ``cellpose.train`` skriver ``<save_path>/models/<name>`` utan suffix, och den mappen innehåller även READMEs och loggar — kontrollen av magiska byte är det som håller en ``README`` utanför modellsamlingen. 4. Allt annat är inte en modell. CSVs, PNGs, ``.npy``-masker och ögonblicksbilder av inställningar hamnar alla här och ignoreras.

records.context: The post-processing of empanada's Panoptic-DeepLab models, ported so spaCR does not depend on empanada-dl. A pixel is mitochondrion when ``semantic`` reaches ``threshold``. Instance centres are the local maxima of ``centres`` in a ``centre_window`` square that reach ``centre_threshold``. Each mitochondrion pixel votes, through its ``offsets`` (row, column), for the place its centre is, and joins the nearest centre found. Instances smaller than ``min_size`` pixels are dropped and the rest are numbered 1..n in raster order of their centres.
records.label: spacr.model_zoo.mitonet_instances#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The post-processing of empanada's Panoptic-DeepLab models, ported so spaCR does not depend on empanada-dl. A pixel is mitochondrion when ``semantic`` reaches ``threshold``. Instance centres are the local maxima of ``centres`` in a ``centre_window`` square that reach ``centre_threshold``. Each mitochondrion pixel votes, through its ``offsets`` (row, column), for the place its centre is, and joins the nearest centre found. Instances smaller than ``min_size`` pixels are dropped and the rest are numbered 1..n in raster order of their centres.
records.translation: Efterbearbetningen från empanadas Panoptic-DeepLab-modeller, portad så att spaCR inte är beroende av empanada-dl. En pixel är mitokondrie när ``semantic`` når ``threshold``. Instanscentrum är de lokala maxima för ``centres`` i en kvadrat av storleken ``centre_window`` som når ``centre_threshold``. Varje mitokondriepixel röstar, via sina ``offsets`` (rad, kolumn), på platsen där dess centrum ligger, och ansluter sig till det närmaste centrum som hittats. Instanser mindre än ``min_size`` pixlar tas bort och resten numreras 1..n i rasterordning efter sina centrum.

records.context: It does not fetch on Qt's main GUI execution path. This function is reached from ``spacr.settings.downloaded_zoo_models`` while a settings panel is being built, so it ran inside ``MainWindow._on_nav_selected`` with nothing able to paint or answer the compositor. Measured with the catalogue host non-routable (10.255.255.1, the shape of a down VPN or a captive portal -- the connect neither completes nor is refused): opening the Mask module took **32.2 s**, all of it a main GUI execution path stuck in ``urlopen``. GNOME asks a window whether it is alive after five seconds, so the user saw GNOME's "force quit" dialog. With the fetch moved off the independent execution path the same open took 2.4 s.

GNOME frågar ett fönster om det lever efter fem sekunder, så användaren såg GNOME:s dialog "force quit". Med hämtningen flyttad från tråden tog samma öppning 2.4 s.

records.context: ``spacr.ml.regression_model`` can return a statsmodels ``OLS``, ``WLS``, ``RLM``, ``QuantReg``, a ``GLM`` in any of six families, a ``MixedLM``, a ``BetaModel``, a sklearn ``Lasso``/``Ridge``/``ElasticNet`` or a ``LinearSVC``. Those objects agree on almost nothing: a sklearn ``Lasso`` has no p-values, no covariance matrix and no ``fittedvalues``; a ``MixedLM`` has no hat matrix; a Gaussian model has no calibration curve worth drawing. Every panel therefore either draws or raises :class:`PanelUnavailable` carrying the *reason*, and the reason is printed on the combined report page and returned in the manifest. A panel is never silently omitted, and never faked with a substitute statistic that does not mean what the axis label says.

records.context: Treating all of those as "the error variance of ``y - fitted``" is how a QC panel reports the wrong microplate sample positions as outliers, in a direction that depends on the units of the response. records.context: Two numbers, because they answer different questions. The *unscaled* condition number is what ``statsmodels`` prints in a summary, and it is dominated by the units of the columns: a predictor measured in cells rather than thousands of cells changes it by 1000 with no change in the science. The *scaled* one (each column normalised to unit length first, the Belsley-Kuh-Welsch definition) is unit-free and is the one whose thresholds — 30, 100, 1000 — mean anything.
records.label: spacr.regression_qc.condition_number#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Two numbers, because they answer different questions. The *unscaled* condition number is what ``statsmodels`` prints in a summary, and it is dominated by the units of the columns: a predictor measured in cells rather than thousands of cells changes it by 1000 with no change in the science. The *scaled* one (each column normalised to unit length first, the Belsley-Kuh-Welsch definition) is unit-free and is the one whose thresholds — 30, 100, 1000 — mean anything.
records.translation: Två tal, eftersom de besvarar olika frågor. Det *oskalade* konditionstalet är det som ``statsmodels`` skriver ut i en sammanfattning, och det domineras av kolumnernas enheter: en prediktor som mäts i celler i stället för tusentals celler ändrar det med 1000 utan någon förändring i vetenskapen. Det *skalade* (varje kolumn först normaliserad till enhetslängd, Belsley-Kuh-Welsch-definitionen) är enhetslöst och är det vars tröskelvärden — 30, 100, 1000 — betyder något.

records.context: ``phi = sum((y - mu)^2 / V(mu)) / df_resid``. Under a correctly specified Poisson model ``phi == 1``. ``phi`` well above 1 means the standard errors are too small by ``sqrt(phi)`` — at ``phi = 6``, a 2.4-fold inflation, which turns noise into a screening experiment full of hits. That is why this number is on the report as a number and not as a shape to eyeball.

records.source: ``phi = sum((y - mu)^2 / V(mu)) / df_resid``. Under a correctly specified Poisson model ``phi == 1``. ``phi`` well above 1 means the standard errors are too small by ``sqrt(phi)`` — at ``phi = 6``, a 2.4-fold inflation, which turns noise into a screen full of hits. That is why this number is on the report as a number and not as a shape to eyeball.
records.translation: ``phi = sum((y - mu)^2 / V(mu)) / df_resid``. Under en korrekt specificerad Poisson-modell gäller ``phi == 1``. Ett ``phi`` långt över 1 betyder att standardfelen är för små med en faktor ``sqrt(phi)`` — vid ``phi = 6`` en 2.4-faldig uppblåsning, vilket förvandlar brus till en screen full av träffar. Det är därför detta tal står i rapporten som ett tal och inte som en form att bedöma med ögat.

records.context: Computed from the inverse of the predictor *correlation* matrix — the identity ``VIF_j = (R^-1)_jj`` — rather than by running ``p`` auxiliary regressions. On a screening experiment design with 1,200 gRNA columns the auxiliary- regression route is ``O(p^4)`` and is impractical; the correlation route is one ``O(p^3)`` decomposition. The two agree exactly when the design contains an intercept (see the test that pins this against ``statsmodels.stats.outliers_influence.variance_inflation_factor``).

records.source: Computed from the inverse of the predictor *correlation* matrix — the identity ``VIF_j = (R^-1)_jj`` — rather than by running ``p`` auxiliary regressions. On a screen design with 1,200 gRNA columns the auxiliary- regression route is ``O(p^4)`` and is impractical; the correlation route is one ``O(p^3)`` decomposition. The two agree exactly when the design contains an intercept (see the test that pins this against ``statsmodels.stats.outliers_influence.variance_inflation_factor``).
records.translation: Beräknas från inversen av prediktorernas *korrelationsmatris* — identiteten ``VIF_j = (R^-1)_jj`` — i stället för genom att köra ``p`` hjälpregressioner. På en screendesign med 1,200 gRNA-kolumner är vägen via hjälpregressioner ``O(p^4)`` och opraktisk; korrelationsvägen är en enda ``O(p^3)``-uppdelning. De två stämmer exakt överens när designen innehåller ett intercept (se testet som fäster detta mot ``statsmodels.stats.outliers_influence.variance_inflation_factor``).

records.context: **A column with no values at all comes back as** ``object``. This is the common one and it is not a data problem: ``pandas.read_sql`` builds the frame from the rows it gets, so a column that is ``NULL`` in every row arrives as a column of ``None`` and pandas types that ``object`` -- even though SQLite declares it ``REAL``. spaCR writes ``NULL`` for a NaN, and whole measurements are legitimately NaN for a whole database: ``skew_intensity``/``kurtosis_intensity`` are NaN for every uniform object, and ``mode_intensity`` was NaN for every object in every database written before the SciPy shim in ``measure._extended_regionprops_table``. Such a column is converted to ``float64`` NaN, which is what it always meant. Nothing is lost, so nothing is warned about -- and the caller's own all-NaN filter then drops it and says so.
records.label: spacr.schema.coerce_model_feature_types#1

records.source: **A column with no values at all comes back as** ``object``. This is the common one and it is not a data problem: ``pandas.read_sql`` builds the frame from the rows it gets, so a column that is ``NULL`` in every row arrives as a column of ``None`` and pandas types that ``object`` -- even though SQLite declares it ``REAL``. spaCR writes ``NULL`` for a NaN, and whole measurements are legitimately NaN for a whole database: ``skew_intensity``/``kurtosis_intensity`` are NaN for every uniform object, and ``mode_intensity`` was NaN for every object in every database written before the SciPy shim in ``measure._extended_regionprops_table``. Such a column is converted to ``float64`` NaN, which is what it always meant. Nothing is lost, so nothing is warned about -- and the caller's own all-NaN filter then drops it and says so.
records.translation: **En kolumn helt utan värden kommer tillbaka som** ``object``. Detta är det vanliga fallet och det är inget dataproblem: ``pandas.read_sql`` bygger ramen från de rader den får, så en kolumn som är ``NULL`` i varje rad anländer som en kolumn med ``None`` och pandas typar den som ``object`` -- trots att SQLite deklarerar den som ``REAL``. spaCR skriver ``NULL`` för ett NaN, och hela mätningar är legitimt NaN för en hel databas: ``skew_intensity``/``kurtosis_intensity`` är NaN för varje likformigt objekt, och ``mode_intensity`` var NaN för varje objekt i varje databas som skrevs före SciPy-mellanlagret i ``measure._extended_regionprops_table``. En sådan kolumn konverteras till ``float64`` NaN, vilket är vad den alltid betydde. Inget går förlorat, så ingen varning ges -- och anroparens eget filter för helt NaN-fyllda kolumner tar sedan bort den och anger det.

records.source: The object prefix is stripped before the label is re-canonicalised, which is what makes this the inverse of :func:`compose_prcfo` for **every** label rather than only the numeric ones. :func:`object_id` reads an already-prefixed numeric id back out of its prefix (``'o7'`` → ``7`` → ``'o7'``), but it cannot do that for a preserved non-numeric token: without stripping, ``'oxy'`` would become ``'ooxy'`` and the key would grow on every pass through the parser.
records.translation: Objektprefixet tas bort innan etiketten görs kanonisk på nytt, vilket är det som gör detta till inversen av :func:`compose_prcfo` för **varje** etikett och inte bara för de numeriska. :func:`object_id` läser tillbaka ett numeriskt id som redan har prefix ur sitt prefix (``'o7'`` → ``7`` → ``'o7'``), men det kan inte göra det för ett bevarat icke-numeriskt token: utan borttagning skulle ``'oxy'`` bli ``'ooxy'`` och nyckeln skulle växa vid varje passage genom tolkaren.
